data.title: From CIIE Exhibit to Patient Access, Gilead's Two Innovative Products Poised for China Approval
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Gilead Sciences is expecting to receive Chinese regulatory approval for two innovative drugs already available to some patients through special-access programs, according to Jin Fangqian, the US biopharmaceutical company’s vice president and China general manager.

Applications for lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injectable human immunodeficiency virus prevention drug, and seladelpar, a treatment for primary biliary cholangitis, are under review, Jin  said at the Ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai.

Lenacapavir offers a more convenient and discreet option for HIV prevention, helping more people at risk , while seladelpar is designed to address unmet needs among PBC patients who don’t have an adequate response to existing treatments or have experienced severe pruritus, helping improve their quality of life, he explained.

Before nationwide approval in China, both products are already available to eligible patients through the Boao Lecheng International Medical Tourism Pilot Zone in Hainan province, while seladelpar is also available in Beijing’s Tianzhu Comprehensive Bonded Zone, according to the company. Jin noted that these two special-access programs can  accumulate real-world data, accelerate approval, and unlock broader clinical use, allowing Chinese patients to benefit earlier from global innovation. 

Their progress represents the broader spillover effect of the CIIE, Jin said. The two drugs, first introduced at a previous CIIE, were among Gilead's highlights at the CIIE last year. 

At this year’s edition, the fifth the firm has attended, it is showcasing further progress, as the company continues to expand its presence in China."The CIIE is a platform that encourages openness, innovation, and cooperation," Jin pointed out. Throughout the years, Gilead has turned many of its innovative products from exhibits into goods, he added.

 

Over the past five editions, a number of Gilead medicines first showcased at the expo have moved from exhibits toward broader patient access in China. Gilead’s antifungal drug AmBisome was included in the China National Essential Medicines List 2026. Coverage of its metastatic breast cancer treatment Trodelvy was expanded to more than 110 city-level supplementary medical insurance catalogs nationwide. Both drugs debuted at the Fifth CIIE in 2022.

 "The CIIE provides an important platform for global innovation to connect with China's healthcare needs," Jin said. "Seeing more innovative medicines move from the expo toward real-world patient access has strengthened our confidence in China and in continuing to bring innovation to Chinese patients."

Building on this progress, Gilead is also increasing the research and development in China. It has nearly 20 clinical projects underway in China, mainly in oncology and inflammatory diseases，covering early- and late-stage trials, Jin said. The company is also expanding partnerships with Chinese biotech firms, from early-stage research through late-stage development, creating more opportunities to integrate China-originated innovation into its global research and development pipeline. 

Gilead began commercial operations in China in 2017. So far, 13 of its medicines have been approved in China, eight of which are included in the National Reimbursement Drug List (NRDL)

At this year's CIIE, Gilead is also holding nearly 20 signing ceremonies and disease education activities covering HIV prevention and treatment, viral hepatitis, PBC, Oncology and Invasive fungal disease, reflecting its continued efforts to connect global innovation, local research and broader collaboration in China. Its 500-square-meter booth also features a patient story zone highlighting how innovation affects patients' lives.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Chinese EV Giant BYD Enters Namibian Market in Global Expansion Drive
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 7 -- Chinese automaker BYD has officially launched its new energy vehicle brand in Namibia, expanding its presence in the African market.

Namibian automotive distributor Pupkewitz Motors announced yesterday that it will represent BYD in the country, with the brand to be offered through retail outlets in Windhoek, Walvis Bay and Ongwediva.

"Our ambition is not simply to introduce new vehicles to the market, but to create an experience around new energy mobility that is relevant to Namibian customers. We look forward to building awareness, educating consumers and allowing customers to experience BYD for themselves," said Nico Pieters, a franchise executive at Pupkewitz Motors, in a statement.

Models being introduced to the Namibian market include the BYD Dolphin, BYD Dolphin Surf, BYD Sealion 5, BYD Sealion 6, BYD Shark 6, BYD Sealion 7 and BYD Seal Performance.

"The range allows Namibian customers to explore different forms of electrified mobility while experiencing the technology, comfort and features associated with the BYD brand," Pieters said.

He said the launch comes as energy efficiency, sustainability and the future of transportation gain increasing attention globally.

"BYD's global focus on new energy technologies places the brand at the forefront of this changing automotive landscape, while its entry into Namibia provides local motorists with greater access to alternative vehicle technologies," he added.

With the official launch of BYD, Pupkewitz Motors is expanding its portfolio to include a global new energy vehicle brand, reinforcing its commitment to providing Namibian customers with greater choice as mobility evolves.

In September, economic and market indicators from Namibian firm IJG Securities, showed that Chinese brands are steadily gaining popularity in Namibia. Haval, Jetour and Chery accounted for 5.9 percent, 5.8 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively, of the Namibian passenger vehicle market.

Editor: Dou Shicong

data.title: China Takes Steps to Speed Up Third-Generation Nuclear Power Rollout
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- China is seeking to accelerate the introduction of its proprietary third-generation nuclear power technology by improving reactor design, digitizing project management, speeding up equipment production, and harmonizing technical standards. The push also involves bringing private investors into projects to widen the funding base and bolster the domestic supply chain.

China General Nuclear Power Group unveiled the Hualong One 2.0, a third-generation pressurized water reactor, in September, featuring improvements in safety, cost-effectiveness, and technological performance.

The upgraded reactor design is intended to boost the efficiency of both project management and construction by 20 percent, with the overall building period capped at 54 months, according to Kan Shuo, deputy director of the Project Management Engineering Technology Support Centre at China Nuclear Engineering Corporation.

At the end of last year, the generating capacity of nuclear power units in commercial operation in China was 62.5 million kilowatts, less than 2 percent of the nation’s total electricity production capacity. This leaves a significant gap to cover to reach the 200-million-kilowatt target projected by the China Nuclear Energy Association for 2040.

Addressing the pressure to meet delivery timelines, Kan noted that in February, China National Nuclear Corporation proposed integrating digital engineering concepts into the design-and-construction process. This allows for seamless flow of data across different project sectors, with the goal of achieving a 20 percent improvement in both management and construction efficiency, and capping the total project duration at 54 months.

The initial delivery estimate for a Hualong One 2.0 reactor was nearly 50 months, said Liu Chang, project management director at First Heavy Industries Dalian Nuclear Power & Petrochemical, a firm responsible for equipment manufacturing. But through process refinement, the delivery time is now expected to be just over 40 months, Liu noted.

Private Capital

In terms of capital, China has begun introducing private investment into nuclear power projects. The San'ao Nuclear Power Plant in Zhejiang province is the first to have private equity participation. The plant is set to have six 1,000-megawatt Hualong One units, with a total projected investment of CNY120 billion (USD17.9 billion).
 

Private investors have a 2 percent stake in the project's first phase, a figure that rises to 30 percent by the third phase, setting a record for the most private funding in China’s nuclear power sector. 

"The participation of private capital has become a key prerequisite for the approval of certain nuclear power projects,” said Xu Lingbin, deputy manager of general management at Cangnan Nuclear Power, which is responsible for building and running the San'ao Nuclear Power Plant.

“Private capital helps supplement the substantial equity funding required for these projects, and private enterprises with strong industrial backgrounds can foster synergy across the upstream and downstream supply chains," Xu told Yicai.

Unified Standards

Efforts are also underway to harmonize standards to facilitate faster project implementation. China’s two major nuclear power conglomerates, CGN and CNNC, previously used different technical standards. 

Efforts to harmonize standards began in 2017, but the alignment did not include a number of equipment components. As of 2024, atomic power industry regulators have pushed for further standardization, encompassing the entire project lifecycle, from design and construction to operation and decommissioning. 

"Promoting the unification of standards is a positive development for the manufacturing sector,” said Gao Dianbao, executive deputy general manager of First Heavy Industries Dalian Nuclear Power, which supplies equipment to both CGN and CNNC. “It streamlines processes and helps unlock production capacity," Gao added.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Hainan Mining Dips After Swedish Unit Is Ordered to Pay USD18.2 Million in Back Taxes, Interest
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Shares in Hainan Mining edged down today after the Chinese mining firm said the Swedish Tax Agency has ordered its Swedish subsidiary to pay more than SEK180 million (USD18.2 million) in back taxes and interest on late payments by Nov. 26 over accounting issues dating back to before Hainan Mining acquired Tethy’s Oil. The company said it plans to challenge the ruling through legal channels.

Hainan Mining’s share price [SHA: 601969] closed down 2.9 percent at CNY8.19 (USD1.20).

The Swedish Tax Agency conducted an audit of Tethys Oil’s corporate income tax filings for 2021 to 2023, Hainan Mining, which bought a controlling stake in the Stockholm-based firm in December 2024, said yesterday. The tax authority concluded that the allocation of operating profits between Tethys Oil and its Oman subsidiary did not comply with the arm’s-length principle, which refers to when the parties of a transaction are independent and on an equal footing.

Hainan Mining said Tethys Oil will review the relevant evidence and seek advice from professional institutions before pursuing legal remedies. The firm has not ruled out initiating legal proceedings with Sweden’s administrative courts, it added.

The ultimate impact of the additional taxes and late-payment interest on Hainan Mining’s annual financial results will be determined based on the findings of its external auditor, it said.

Hainan Mining was founded in 2007 by Fosun Group and Hainan Haigang Group, and went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2014. It is currently the only mainland-listed company with business operations spanning both mineral resources and energy, it said.

In the first nine months, Hainan Mining’s net profit attributable to shareholders more than doubled from the year before to CNY650 million (USD97.4 million), while revenue soared 31.6 percent to CNY4.4 billion (USD660 million).

Hainan Mining acquired a 51 percent stake in Australia’s Roc Oil from Chinese conglomerate Fosun International in 2019 and the remaining 49 percent in 2023, for a combined consideration of approximately USD393 million.

Roc Oil launched a takeover bid for Tethys Oil in September 2024 and completed its acquisition of a controlling stake in December that year, after which Tethys Oil was delisted. Tethys Oil holds significant onshore oil assets in Oman, with mining rights covering about 60,000 square kilometers, equivalent to around 18 percent of the country’s land area.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Increasing Car Weight by 20% Leads to Double Damage to Roads, Nio CEO Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Vehicle weight issues directly affect Nio's technological approach, because even a 1.2-time increase to the standard will cause more than double the damage to road pavements, according to the chief executive officer of electric vehicle startup Nio.

Based on the "fourth power law" in road engineering, the structural damage vehicles cause to roads is proportional to the fourth power of axle load, with 1.2 to the fourth being about 2.07, Li Bin, who is also founder and chairman of Nio, said at an auto forum during the World Internet Conference yesterday.

In addition, Li and Li Shufu, chairman of Geely Holding Group, held their first public dialogue at the forum after teaming up on battery charging and swapping on Sept. 28. Their conversation focused on the lifespan of power batteries and the route of energy replenishment, with Li Bin raising the issue of vehicle weight.

Nio's battery packs usually weigh 400 to 500 kilograms, Li Bin said, noting that the lighter weight means the company must accept constraints such as smaller battery pack capacity and shorter range and continue to seek solutions under these conditions.

On July 6 last year, Li said during a livestream that the auto industry has improved EVs' range by expanding battery capacity, but "heavier cars cause greater damage to roads, so many countries base taxes on vehicle weight," with the topic briefly trending on social media.

"If more than 300 million cars in China become heavy-duty vehicles, the roads will be crushed," Li told Yicai in May this year, calling for national restrictions on vehicle weight. "Without national guidance, the industry will engage in disorderly competition."

The average curb weight of new passenger vehicles in China was 1,704 kilograms in 2024, up from 1,312 kg in 2012, according to data from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The increase in new energy passenger vehicles is even more pronounced, with the figure reaching 1,939 kg in the first four months of this year, industry statistics showed.

Regulators are also following up with relevant measures, linking EVs' energy consumption limits to their curb weight starting Jan. 1 this year, and imposing stricter limits for vehicles weighing 2,710 kg or above. From the same day, buyers of new energy vehicles must pay half of the standard auto purchase tax, instead of receiving a full exemption.

Competent authorities have begun discussing a tax system reform based on vehicle weight, Yicai learned.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: DeepSeek Harness Releases DAU Data for First Time, Topping 1.5 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Chinese artificial intelligence giant DeepSeek has released user data for DeepSeek Harness for the first time, revealing that the open-source agent harness framework has more than 1.5 million daily active users.

DeepSeek Harness had 1.54 million DAUs on its official application programming interface over the week ended Nov. 4, up from 429,000 over the week ended Oct. 7 and 271,000 over the one ended Sept. 30, Hangzhou-based DeepSeek said yesterday. Users consume around 92 trillion tokens a day.

The number of third-party plug-ins has surged to about 35,000 since DeepSeek Harness was released, and about 60 percent of users created or installed at least one third-party plugin. It is preparing a support program for plugin authors.

DeepSeek Harness is a software support framework built around large language models, designed to help AI agents manage and execute more complex tasks. It can be seen as a complete set of operating systems an LLM needs to truly become an agent.

As a benchmark for domestic LLMs, DeepSeek is accelerating evolution. On Oct. 31, DeepSeek Harness’ team published a technical article called ‘Exploring Super-Agent Design to a More Autonomous Agent System’ on its official WeChat account.

The article claims that improved model capabilities have given rise to new applications, and personal agents have begun to emerge rapidly. However, mainstream agent design still cannot support this mode at the multi-task and team-collaboration level, and the multi-task limit depends on people’s attention.

To overcome these limitations, it is necessary to break the binding between agents and a one-off manual session, making it a continuous entity that can maintain context across sessions and simultaneously advance multiple complex tasks without interfering with each other. DeepSeek refers to this form of agent and its system architecture as ‘super-agent.’

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: [CIIE] China-EU Ties Have ‘Unparalleled Foundation,’ ACEA’s Beijing Representative Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- China and the European Union have an “unparalleled foundation for cooperation” on intelligent connected vehicles, new energy, and safety, according to the chief representative of the Beijing office of the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association.

The ACEA will fully leverage its unique strengths to build a bridge for exchanges between Chinese and foreign parties through four types of activities during the Ninth China International Import Expo, Zhang Shuo told Yicai in an exclusive interview.

The four types of activities are inviting Chinese automobile industry regulators and research institutions to engage in face-to-face dialogue with international companies, facilitating exchanges between Chinese and international carmakers and between leading Chinese suppliers and foreign firms, holding industry dialogues and forums focused on the ultra-luxury vehicle and commercial vehicle segments, and providing dedicated exhibition spaces for member companies, such as Volvo Trucks, Aston Martin, and Jeep.

Representing 18 major global automakers, the ACEA is officially participating in the CIIE in Shanghai for the first time this year. Its booth focuses on two key niche markets -- ultra-luxury vehicles and commercial vehicles -- and will host two high-level forum dialogues.

“New energy is a global trend, but meeting different customer needs through diversified products is a sign of a mature market,” Zhang noted. “Although both digital watches and mobile phones can tell the time, there will always be people who prefer mechanical watches.

“China’s huge automotive market and its overall economic growth prospects are the foundation and source of appeal for international luxury automakers’ focus on China,” he added.

Last year, China and Europe accounted for about 54 percent of global auto production and 52 percent of global vehicle registrations, according to data shared by Zhang. “In other words, any decision made by China and Europe will affect the shape of the global automotive industry.”

Moreover, China and the EU are almost completely aligned in their major automotive industry goals, Zhang said. In autonomous driving and intelligent connected vehicles, they have made major moves in policy and regulatory development while advancing large-scale demonstration applications this year.

More importantly, the product access systems implemented by China and the EU are similar, and many of the national standards they cite are the same, he noted. Both of them are active participants in the international harmonization of automotive technical regulations under the United Nations framework.

“In the next decade, artificial intelligence will give us endless room for imagination when it comes to automotive products themselves, as it becomes further integrated and coordinated with cars, transportation, smart homes, and the telecom industry,” Zhang pointed out.

The auto industry, as a pillar of the national economy and a labor-intensive sector, supports a large number of jobs. He called on governments to support the auto industry more, not by imposing more restrictions, but by creating an open, inclusive, and fair environment.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s Geely, Nio Strengthen Battery-Swap Alliance With Cross-Shareholding Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 28 -- Chinese automotive giant Geely Holding Group and electric vehicle manufacturer Nio will deepen their strategic cooperation on battery swapping and EV charging through a cross-shareholding arrangement at the subsidiary level, aimed at accelerating the expansion of their battery-swap and charging service networks.

Geely will use its 100 percent equity in its battery-swap service provider Yiyi Internet Technology and CNY640 million (USD95.3 million) in cash to subscribe to newly issued shares in Nio’s battery-swap and charging unit Nio Power, Shanghai-based Nio said today. Upon completion of the transaction, Geely will hold a 30 percent stake in Nio Power, which will have a post-investment valuation of CNY16 billion (USD2.4 billion).

Nio was one of the earliest Chinese EV manufacturers to adopt battery swapping and set up Nio Power in 2017 to develop and run a battery-swap and charging service network. As of Sept. 20, Nio operated 4,099 battery-swap stations and 5,289 charging stations, and had provided users with over 120 million battery swaps in total, it said.

Yiyi, founded in 2017, managed more than 470 battery-swap stations in over 40 cities across China as of April last year, and has plans to expand to 2,000 stations by next year, according to its website.

The integration of Yiyi into Nio Power will accelerate the expansion of Nio's battery swapping network, with the aim of building 10,000 battery-swap stations by 2030, Nio said. The two sides will also work together to establish unified battery-swapping technology standards, while Hangzhou-based Geely will develop battery-swap vehicles models for consumers.

Nio will also acquire a stake in Geely’s EV charging service provider Zhejiang Haohan Energy Technology, according to the agreement between the two parties. Upon completion of the transaction, Nio will hold a 10 percent stake in Haohan, and both sides will share resources to expand charging network coverage and improve operational efficiency.

Haohan currently operates 2,500 charging stations and 12,000 charging guns in 232 cities across China. By the end of 2027, it plans to expand its network to 22,000 charging stations and 100,000 charging guns, Geely said.

The collaboration between Nio and Geely dates back to November 2023, when Nio announced plans to form a battery swapping alliance with automakers. Since then, it has established partnerships with eight automakers, including Changan Automobile and Geely.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Hongqiao Forum Releases New Recommendations Report for Trading Partners Seeking to Tap Vast Chinese Market
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- The Hongqiao International Economic Forum, held during the China International Import Expo, unveiled the first Export-to-China Capacity Development Report, offering targeted suggestions for trading partners seeking access to the country’s supersized market.

The report, released yesterday at the Hongqiao Forum -- a high-level dialogue platform that focuses on global openness, economic governance, and open cooperation among political, business, and academic leaders -- featured two chapters: Sharing the Opportunities of China’s Large Market With the World and Jointly Boosting Capacity for Exports to China.

The Institute of World Economics and Politics of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences compiled the first chapter, analyzing trading partners’ export conditions to China and outlining concrete measures the country has rolled out to expand imports from all countries. The Division of International Trade and Commodities of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development prepared the second chapter, selecting 10 of China’s trading partners, examining their respective performance and export potential, and offering suggestions to strengthen their export capacity for the Chinese market.

The report tailors differentiated recommendations for exports to China based on the realities of trading partners, helping countries translate their product strengths into tangible export capacity, said Liao Fan, director of the Institute of World Economics and Politics. Updated editions will be released annually to track changes in Chinese market demand and trading partners’ export capacity, while refining and enriching its analytical framework, Liao said.

“This report represents another important public good provided by China to advance global trade cooperation,” noted Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong.

The mix of goods exported to China worldwide is gradually shifting from a past pattern where industrial products held an absolutely dominant position to a structure led by industrial products, supplemented by resource goods and agricultural products, with intermediate goods gaining greater prominence, the report said. Major intermediate goods with high import value include crude oil, iron ore, and processors, controllers, and memories in integrated circuits.

The rising share of intermediate goods reflects China’s evolving role in the global supply chain: from a simple processor reliant on imported capital and manufactured goods to a deep integrator of full supply chains that absorbs global energy resources, intermediate goods, and high-tech inputs, the report added.

Final consumer goods shipped to China feature a diversified product portfolio. Categories posting rapid growth in recent years include food, beauty and personal care items, pharmaceuticals, and electronics. By contrast, textiles and apparel, certain vehicle types, and low-end food products have declined, driven by shifts in the country’s domestic consumption structure and by supply and price differentials between the local and overseas markets.

The report highlighted feed grains and high-quality agricultural products, basic energy resources, critical minerals for the new energy sector, semiconductor and electronic intermediate goods, high-end manufacturing equipment, precision instruments, and healthcare and pharmaceutical consumer goods as promising areas for future exports to China.

China’s vast market generates demand not only for advanced manufactured goods but also for resource commodities and specialty agricultural products, making it an inclusive market for economies at different stages of development, Liao pointed out, adding that the country boasts massive market space and an increasingly open door.

China has remained the world’s second-largest importer for 17 consecutive years, with its goods imports surging 27 percent in eight months ended Aug. 31 from a year earlier, while the full-year figure is expected to top USD3 trillion for the first time, the report said. Its share of received global exports climbed to 9.2 percent last year from 3.2 percent in 2000. Exports to China account for over 59 percent of the total outbound shipments of sampled Belt and Road partner countries.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: China’s Tinci Inks Long-Term Deal to Supply Lithium Battery Electrolytes to Eve Energy
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Tinci Materials Technology, a leading Chinese supplier of electrolytes and electrolyte chemicals for lithium batteries, has signed a long-term supply deal with Chinese lithium battery giant Eve Energy.

Tinci’s factory in Jiujiang, eastern Jiangxi province, will sell a total of 450,000 tons of lithium battery electrolyte products to Eve Energy from 2027 to 2029, the Guangzhou-based supplier announced later yesterday. Details such as the unit price and quality standards will be confirmed in purchase orders and quality agreements that the pair will sign in the future.

Tinci did not reveal the total value of the deal, but based on current lithium iron phosphate battery electrolyte prices of about CNY30,000 (USD4,500) per ton, it could bring the firm about CNY13.5 billion (USD2 billion) in sales revenue.

Tinci’s shares [SHE: 002709] were trading down 0.5 percent at CNY28.86 (USD4.32) as of 1.05 p.m. today, after earlier gaining as much as 3.2 percent. The Shenzhen Component Index fell 1.7 percent.

Tinci is the world’s leading supplier of lithium battery electrolytes. It previously signed long-term supply deals with four major Chinese lithium battery makers -- Cornex New Energy, Gotion High-Tech, Rept Battero, and China Lithium Battery Technology -- locking in a combined supply volume of over 1.7 million tons.

Tinci sold more than 720,000 tons of lithium battery electrolyte last year, an increase of about 44 percent from 2024, seizing a global market share of more than 32 percent.

In addition to its plants in China, Tinci has original equipment manufacturing partner factories in the United States and Germany, which have already started supplying local customers. The company is also investing in new plants in the US and Morocco, according to its latest annual financial report.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Most Chinese Firms Are Willing to Hike AI Investment, Accenture Survey Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Chinese companies continue to welcome the arrival of the artificial intelligence era, with more than half willing to increase future investment in the technology, according to a new survey by global consulting giant Accenture.

The survey, which included 200 executives, found that some 57 percent of firms will use new budgets to support AI investments, according to the findings Accenture released at the ninth China International Import Expo, which kicked off yesterday. About 23 percent said AI can deliver the most value in efficiency this year, followed by productivity at 20 percent, innovation at 18 percent, and revenue growth at 16 percent.

On the token economy, about 43 percent of respondents said they are familiar with the concept and actively manage costs through different measures, including 61 percent optimizing AI systems, 46 percent establishing governance and supervision mechanisms, and 45 percent monitoring AI use and cost. However, the percentage of companies actively deploying AI agents fell to 24 percent from 26 percent in a survey conducted earlier this year.

New quality productive forces driven by AI innovation are improving the operational efficiency of Chinese firms and starting to reshape their products, processes, organizations, and business models, said Samantha Zhu, chairwoman of Accenture China. AI amplifies companies' insights, decision-making, and operational capabilities, making it more likely to achieve cross-market resource allocation, she added.

In addition, the survey questioned 200 employees, who indicated that AI has enhanced their work experience and satisfaction. Some 85 percent said using AI has improved their job satisfaction, with 23 percent using AI tools every day, while 44 percent noted that AI agents can complete tasks from start to finish without human supervision. However, only 9 percent believe their companies are achieving widespread and sustainable business value through AI investment.

Half of employees said the rapid development of AI and related technologies makes it hard to keep up, while 49 percent added that AI training is too theoretical to guide real-life work.

On the biggest limiting factor for companies to achieve AI value, about 21 percent of executives pointed to a lack of integration between AI projects and core business strategies, 17 percent to the complexity of integrating AI into business processes, and 16 percent to a lack of skilled talent.

Accenture, which has participated in the CIIE for seven consecutive years, brought the first AI Center of Excellence solution launched in China to the expo this year, helping companies evaluate AI investment and translate it into measurable business results. Its Nexus enterprise ontology platform helps firms connect data and knowledge resources, enhance intelligent decision-making, risk management, and operational collaboration capabilities, and provide foundational support for large-scale deployment of AI agents and the development of autonomous operation systems.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: Yicai’s Wenhai AI Agent Debuts at CIIE News Center
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- Yicai Media Group's self-developed Wenhai Agent debuted in the Artificial Intelligence Park zone of the news center at the ninth China International Import Expo, which kicked off yesterday, providing international journalists and firms attending the event with the latest and most reputable news, research reports, and policy briefings from around the world.

Multiple reporters covering the CIIE praised the professionalism and accuracy of the Wenhai Agent's outputs after testing it. A Moldovan journalist said she received the latest information on the country's economic conditions from the tool, while an Iranian peer said the response she got on market opportunities for Iranian goods in China was highly consistent with her understanding.

Built on Yicai's Xingyi AI Model, the Wenhai Agent is designed primarily for Chinese and foreign companies with global operations. Drawing on world news feeds, authoritative reports, policies and regulations, academic papers, and compliant commercial datasets, it delivers well-organized professional insights from simple user prompts.

The Wenhai Agent ingests on average more than 3,000 multilingual real-time news articles a day. Its coverage spans policy updates, market shifts, and industrial trends across more than 180 countries and regions, ensuring a timely and broad reach for global financial and economic updates and serving as Yicai's extended international information gateway in the intelligent media era and a smart hub for up-to-date global financial news.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: Data, Computing Power, Chip Capacity, Energy, Minerals to Be World’s Core Resources, Unitree Robotics CEO Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- The five most critical resources for the world going forward will be data, computing power, chip capacity, energy, and minerals, with computing power competition being "extremely fierce," according to the chief executive and founder of leading Chinese humanoid robot maker Unitree Robotics.

"The five resource categories will constitute the world's most essential assets in the future," Wang Xingxing said while sharing his insights on the future development of the robotics industry at a sub-forum themed "Humanoid Robots and Embodied Intelligence Industry" at the ninth Hongqiao International Economic Forum held yesterday. Competition in the artificial intelligence sector is gradually expanding to the underlying resources that underpin AI development, moving beyond rivalry over models and algorithms, he noted.

On the technological outlook for humanoid robots and embodied intelligence, Wang said the key challenge is no longer whether a model can comprehend instructions, but whether it can translate that understanding into precise physical motion. For example, the world's top multimodal models have a success rate close to 100 percent when tasked with having robots grasp relatively large objects, but that drops when used for more delicate operations, such as picking up mechanical components, he noted.

The core challenge stems from insufficient input-output alignment between multimodal models and the physical world, Wang pointed out, adding that even if a model understands task requirements, the robot's execution may still carry errors of several millimeters. For high-precision scenarios like industrial manufacturing, any deviations can directly cause operational failure, he stressed.

Once the alignment error is resolved, embodied AI foundation models will face few major technical hurdles for real-world deployment, Wang said. Remaining challenges will mainly involve engineering and commercial rollout, and the technical bottleneck is likely to be addressed within the next one to two years, he added.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: US Manufacturers Debut New Products at CIIE to Seize New Opportunities in China
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 6 -- US manufacturers have brought products covering industrial digitalization, green energy, and high-end equipment to the Ninth China International Import Expo, which is not only a platform for showcasing technology but also an important channel for meeting China's manufacturing upgrading needs and expanding cooperation.

GE Vernova is showcasing its 9HA and 6F.03 gas turbines and its LM6000 VELOX aeroderivative gas turbine, which can generate power using 100 percent hydrogen, as well as its direct air capture and carbon capture and storage technologies. The US energy company is also hosting the Asia debut of its low-carbon energy transition sand table, which presents power system solutions for different scenarios in northwestern, central, and southeastern China.

Honeywell Technologies, which has attended all nine CIIE editions, is participating in the expo under its new brand after the spin-off from Honeywell, now focusing on its Forge intelligent connected platform and artificial intelligence-driven industry innovation solutions.

More than 20 signings will take place at the CIIE, said Yu Feng, president of Honeywell Technologies China, adding that the 500-square-meter booth showcases the results of cooperation with more than 200 partners.

Honeywell Technologies is also displaying seven products making their China debuts, spanning the semiconductor, data center, smart hotel, marine and offshore engineering, low-carbon energy, energy storage and new energy vehicles, smart healthcare, and smart manufacturing sectors.

Rockwell Automation is showing the CompactLogix 5390 controller for the first time in the world at the CIIE. It has also brought the ControlLogix 5590 controller and the FactoryTalk ResilientEdge execution architecture. The new products focus on cybersecurity, integrated safety, and improved control performance.

Meeting China's Industrial Upgrading Needs

For US companies, the Chinese market is an important part of their global business layout and a key market for applying new technologies and innovating products.

"The CIIE is not only a platform for showcasing advanced technologies and achievements, but also one where we can feel the pulse of the market and advance hand in hand with our partners," said Xu Xin, chairman of GE Energy Investment China.

Honeywell Technologies’ commitment to deepening its presence in China will not change, regardless of the circumstances, Yu said. The firm has 10 research and development engineering centers in the country, and its newest innovation center has joined Pudong New Area's Group Open Innovation initiative.

China's fast-iterating, high-standard market demand, continuously unfolding engineering dividends, and extremely rich application scenarios make it fertile ground for innovation, Yu pointed out.

As the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) begins, manufacturing is accelerating its digital, intelligent, green, and integrated development, said Ian Shih, president of Rockwell Automation China. Companies' focus is shifting from improving the efficiency of a machine or production line to using data and AI to connect different levels and factories, so that practices proven effective in one plant can be replicated in others, he added.

Cooperation is also extending from product displays to technology development in overseas markets. GE Vernova is working with China Huadian on hydrogen-blending combustion retrofits, and with China Machinery Engineering to expand into the Nigerian power market. Its project in Anji, China’s Zhejiang province, jointly developed with CHN Energy Investment Group, has begun operation.

Rockwell Automation has collected more than 500 industrial use cases across more than 100 industrial sub-sectors through its Climate Lighthouse initiative and is helping Chinese companies take their practical experience overseas.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Chinese Universities Hand Out Free Tokens as AI Becomes Campus Essential
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 3 -- (Yicai) Nov. 3 -- Chinese universities are increasingly handing out free artificial intelligence tokens to cut students' computing costs as surging demand turns AI computing platforms into essential campus infrastructure.


 

Hefei's University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) was the first to announce a free daily allowance of 100 million tokens for every faculty member and student in the middle of this year, Yicai learned. Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (BUPT) followed in September by opening free computing accounts for nearly 10,000 new students, while Shanghai's Tongji University began offering all faculty and students 100 million tokens a week last week.


 

The giveaways reflect a broader shift toward making AI a basic campus resource, much like libraries and computer labs, as universities invest in computing infrastructure to lower research costs and widen access to advanced technology.


 

Computing power could soon become as important to universities as libraries and sports facilities, according to Xue Lan, dean of Tsinghua University's Schwarzman College. Speaking at the recent University of Hong Kong Talent Forum in Beijing, he said computing platforms, large language model data centers, intelligent tutors, and high-performance networks may become the defining infrastructure of universities in the future.


 

Free token allowances help students cut the cost of running code and developing AI agents. USTC's daily allocation of 100 million tokens per person, which expires and resets each day, provides access to mainstream models including DeepSeek-V4, Zhipu AI's GLM5.2, and Alibaba's Qwen series. At market prices, the allowance is worth several dozen yuan (at least USD3) per student per day.


 

Universities Expand AI Computing Infrastructure


 

Beyond handing out free tokens, Chinese universities are investing in their own computing infrastructure to give students direct access to AI tools.


 

In September, BUPT launched its "Everyone Has Computing Power" platform, giving nearly 10,000 incoming undergraduate and graduate students free access to more than 10 LLMs and AI agents. Each student gets a dedicated virtual server they can configure independently, with AI models already installed and ready to use for tasks such as developing their own agents.


 

Some are going further. Shanghai Jiao Tong University has developed Zhiyuan No. 1, China's largest domestically developed university AI computing platform. Nanjing's Southeast University has established the country's first university-level AI computing center built entirely with domestic technology.


 

Sichuan University has also teamed up with telecoms giant China Unicom to construct a data center and a high-speed computing network connecting its four campuses.


 

Greater access to AI could also help students become more versatile, according to Li Hongyang, assistant dean of HKU's School of Computing and Data Science. He said the AI era demands talent who can combine technical expertise with business acumen.


 

Li encouraged young people to use LLMs to fill gaps in their knowledge and develop a broader range of skills.


 

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Alibaba Cloud Powers Africa’s First Olympic Event in Bid to Win Overseas Markets
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 3 -- Alibaba Cloud has built Senegal’s first dedicated Olympic cloud infrastructure to support the ongoing 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympic event to be held on African soil, as the cloud computing arm of Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding seeks to capture a larger share of overseas markets by showcasing its technologies and capabilities through high-profile international sporting events.

The private cloud will be handed over to Senegal in its entirety after the Games and converted into a national cloud platform to support the country’s ongoing digital development needs, according to the project plan. As Chinese cloud service providers accelerate their overseas expansion, the delivery of a cloud platform for a major sporting event in Africa is emerging as a strategic opportunity for Chinese vendors to establish a foothold in the international private cloud market.

““If we’re talking about this project alone, we might just manage to break even,” Liu Guohua, vice president of Alibaba Cloud, recently told Yicai and other media outlets. “However, revenue from Alibaba Cloud’s international private cloud business nearly doubled in the first half, significantly outpacing growth in the Chinese market.”

Alibaba Cloud is providing cloud-based broadcasting for the Games, as well as supporting a ticketing system capable of handling millions of tickets, electronic visa processing and a one-stop service platform for athletes, Liu said. The Hangzhou-based company has also helped Senegal transition from paper-based visas to electronic visas. All these systems run on the dedicated Olympic cloud infrastructure built by Alibaba Cloud for the event.

Unlike public cloud services, which allow customers to access shared computing resources, private clouds are deployed in environments designated by individual clients and tailored to their specific requirements.

Alibaba Cloud does not yet have a public cloud node in Senegal. Taking into account the country's power supply and network infrastructure, the company's private cloud team will deploy the cloud computing operating system in a local environment for this Youth Olympic Games. After the event, the entire platform will be handed over to the Senegalese government and repurposed as the country's national cloud.

Rather than simply selling cloud resources, Alibaba Cloud is using major sporting events as an opportunity to package its technology and capabilities into comprehensive cloud platforms, positioning itself to capture a larger share of overseas markets.

"It is not that many countries are unwilling to adopt advanced technology but rather that they do not know how to use it or how to make it part of their own national technological infrastructure," Liu said.

The rising emphasis on data control and digital infrastructure in various countries is creating new opportunities in the cloud market. US market research firm Gartner predicts that global spending on sovereign cloud infrastructure-as-a-service will surge 35.6 percent this year from last year to reach USD80 billion. This is about three times the growth rate of the overall private cloud market. Sovereign cloud IaaS expenditure in the Middle East and Africa is estimated to soar 89 percent this year.

"International business may still account for less than 5 percent of our entire private cloud business, but the resources allocated to it are close to 50 percent of the whole sector's total investment," Liu said.

Building a stronger competitive position in the rapidly expanding overseas private cloud market is becoming a key strategic focus for cloud service providers, he added.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: [In Photos] Humanoid Robots Move Beyond Demos to Take Photos, Brew Tea, Serve Guests at CIIE
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 5 -- Humanoid robots are taking on real-world tasks at this year's China International Import Expo, which opened today, marking a shift from demonstrations of physical agility to practical applications.

Unlike at previous editions of the CIIE, humanoid robots are no longer just showing off their ability to walk, jump, and perform complex movements. They are also beginning to understand human needs, operate real tools, and interact smoothly with their surroundings, Yicai observed at the venue.

Launched in 2018 to open China's market and boost imports, the annual CIIE runs through Nov. 10 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai.

Singapore-headquartered robotics company Sharpa is taking customized photos for journalists from around the world at the expo's media center. To complete the task, the robot must pick up a camera, adjust its grip, aim at the subject, and press the shutter in sequence, company staff told Yicai. The process tests the capabilities of its dexterous hand while placing greater demands on its perception abilities.

Hitch Open, a global competition platform for autonomous driving and robotics AI, showcased a robot capable of playing table tennis against a human opponent without remote control or human intervention.

Crystal Tang, global executive chair of Hitch Open, told Yicai that the robot uses the AgiBot Expedition A3 humanoid platform and is equipped with HITTER, a humanoid robot table tennis system developed by the FHL Vive Center for Enhanced Reality at the University of California, Berkeley. The robot has achieved a rally of 106 consecutive shots against a human opponent.

Five photos were selected:

https://www.yicai.com/news/103426551.html

Pic 1 (2/6): A Sharpa robot taking photos of journalists.

Pic 2 (3/6): An AgiBot robot "tea master" brewing tea on site.

Pic 3 (4/6): A Hitch Open table tennis robot playing against a human opponent.

Pic 4 (5/6): A Tesla robot capable of carrying luggage, walking dogs, and sorting items.

Pic 5 (6/6): An AgiBot robot serving as a "hotel butler," interacting with guests, entering their information into the hotel system, and delivering room key cards.

data.title: Danone Opens Second China R&D Hub to Drive Specialized Nutrition Growth
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 5 -- Danone inaugurated its Shanghai R&D and Innovation Centre on Nov. 2, marking the opening of the French food giant’s second R&D hub in China. The facility houses the company’s third gut microbiome laboratory worldwide and is a key part of its nutrition business strategy in the Asia-Pacific region.

The newly opened Shanghai center extends beyond traditional R&D functions. While Danone’s Open Science Research Centre for Life-transforming Nutrition, launched in 2020, focuses on breast milk research, gut health as well as food safety and quality, the Shanghai facility also houses a 700-square-metre pilot production plant and a 300-square-metre space dedicated to science demonstrations and consumer engagement. These facilities are intended to accelerate the translation of research findings into market-ready products and provide the space for them to be tested and validated.

The gut microbiome laboratory is the center’s most significant investment, according to sources. The lab will generate billions of data points, and with China’s advanced data infrastructure and artificial intelligence capabilities, the firm will be able to extract valuable insights more quickly, Le Xintao, vice president of R&D and innovation for Danone Asia-Pacific and China, told Yicai.

Meanwhile, China’s innovation ecosystem and vast consumer market will allow Danone to test product solutions more rapidly and assess how well they meet consumer needs. The Paris-based company will then share these insights and findings with its global R&D and innovation network.

Danone’s substantial investment in local R&D comes as the Chinese market undergoes significant changes. The firm’s Chief Financial Officer Juergen Esser previously disclosed that China accounts for one-third of Danone’s infant nutrition revenue.

A declining birth rate has slowed growth in China’s infant formula market, which is now worth around EUR20 billion (USD22.5 billion).

As competition intensifies in an increasingly saturated market, rivalry has shifted from branding and distribution channels to advanced formulations and scientific evidence, Song Liang, an independent dairy industry analyst, told Yicai. This transition requires substantial investment in capital, technology and talent, putting companies’ overall strength and R&D capabilities to the test.

Danone sees specialized nutrition as its next major growth opportunity in China. Over the past few years, the firm has set up specialized medical nutrition plants in Qingdao and Changsha. In October 2025, it carried out a modernization and expansion project at its existing production facility in Wuxi.

In the first three quarters, Danone’s sales in the Asia-Pacific region climbed 4.9 percent from the year before to EUR4.7 billion (USD5.2 billion), making it the company’s fastest-growing region. Revenue from its specialized nutrition business in the Asia-Pacific region jumped 7.9 percent to EUR1.1 billion (USD1.2 billion) over the same period. Esser said at the earnings call that the Chinese market made an outsized contribution to the category’s performance.

Against this backdrop, Danone’s management is optimistic about the long-term growth prospects of China’s nutrition sector. The firm estimates that China’s population aged 60 and above will reach 300 million by 2030 and 350 million by 2040, fueling further demand for medical nutrition products among older consumers.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China’s Jereh Lands USD2.7 Billion Oil and Gas Service Projects in UAE
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 5 -- Jereh Group has secured three oil and gas services projects in the United Arab Emirates from a unit of Abu Dhabi National Oil Company that together are worth as much as USD2.7 billion, bolstering the Chinese energy services and equipment provider’s position in the Middle East market.

Jereh Oil & Gas Engineering Corporation-Abu Dhabi was awarded the projects by ADNOC Onshore, with work expected to start after contracts are signed, its Yantai-based parent company announced yesterday, citing the client’s letter of acceptance.

The first project, worth up to USD1.7 billion, will be delivered under a design-build-operate model, covering surface works for the Ruwais Diyab unconventional natural gas field in the Ruwais region, with a construction period of 29 months. Jereh Oil & Gas will be responsible for the design, procurement, construction, and commissioning of facilities and pipelines and will run the project for five years after it goes into production.

The second project, worth about USD600 million, will involve the Bab and North East Bab oilfields, with an estimated execution period of five years, while the third project will involve the Bu Hasa, Bida Qimzan, and Huwaila oilfields. It is worth about USD393 million and has a three-year service period.

The second and third awards are One Tie-In projects at ADNOC Onshore's existing oilfields. Under this arrangement, the owner issues phased orders according to its oilfield development plans.

The second project’s scope includes connecting newly drilled production wells to the oilfield’s existing infrastructure, as well as retrofitting or dismantling of surface facilities for existing wells, aiming to shorten the time for new wellhead hookups and retrofitting of surface facilities for existing wells. The third project only covers connection of new wellheads.

Ruwais Diyab is ADNOC Onshore’s first large unconventional natural gas project, Jereh said. Securing the award represents the comprehensive deployment in the Middle East of Jereh's integrated capabilities, spanning proprietary unconventional gas extraction and transportation technologies, production equipment manufacturing, digital production management, and efficient operations and maintenance services, it said.

Winning the biddingg for the two other projects further deepens the cooperation between the two companies after Jereh Oil & Gas secured the contract for ADNOC Onshore’s well digital renovation project last year, reflecting the client’s continued recognition of the supplier’s professional service capabilities in oil and gas extraction and performance in contract fulfillment, Jereh noted.

In February last year, Jereh Oil & Gas inked a USD920 million deal with ADNOC Onshore to oversee a project involving the intelligent transformation of various wellhead facilities in the client’s Bab, Bu Hasa, and South East oilfields. Once the project is completed, the fields are expected to operate without the need for personnel to be continuously stationed on site.

Jereh has actively expanded overseas in recent years. In addition to ADNOC, it has established long-term partnerships with other Middle Eastern oil and gas giants such as Saudi Aramco and Kuwait National Petroleum Company.

After climbing by as much as 3 percent in Shenzhen this morning, Jereh’s shares [SHE: 002353] closed down 1.9 percent at CNY88.27 (USD13.24) each. The stock staged a late-session rally yesterday, surging by its 10 percent daily trading limit to end at CNY90.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s Exhibition Area at World Travel Market Is Largest Ever This Year
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 5 -- China's exhibition area at the 2026 World Travel Market in London has set a new record high since the country joined the world’s most influential travel and tourism event.

China’s exhibition area at this year’s WTM is 487.5 square meters, up about 22 percent from last year’s edition. It features cultural and tourism departments and enterprises from 14 provincial-level regions, with 116 exhibitors, including many new faces such as Legoland Shanghai Resort, which is owned by UK investor Merlin Entertainments Group.

The 2026 WTM kicked off at Excel London, Europe’s largest fully integrated convention and exhibition center, on Nov. 3 and will run through today. This year’s event has attracted over 4,000 exhibitors from more than 180 countries and regions.

UK tourists are more willing to visit China after the visa-free policy was implemented. Beijing received nearly 100,000 tourists from the United Kingdom in the first seven months of the year, up over 53 percent from a year earlier, said Jonathan Heastie, head of tourism at the WTM’s organizer RX.

More and more travelers are seeking immersive experiences and hope to know local people and understand local culture, Heastie noted, adding that specialty cuisine, vibrant traditional customs, and the opportunity to get to know a place through locals are exactly what China offers.

The task of tourism practitioners is to help clients explore more possibilities in Chinese tourism, such as not being limited to one city, exploring multiple regions, and extending their stay, he added.

Many Chinese cities are not well known overseas, and many foreign tourists lack knowledge of Chinese travel destinations, David Haigh, chairman of Brand Finance, said at the opening ceremony of the WTM’s China exhibition area, about some challenges the Chinese tourism industry faces.

The Chinese ice and snow exhibition attracted a large crowd of visitors. Many UK people attending the WTM were curious and wanted to learn more. However, it will be hard for China to become a viable winter travel destination for UK tourists.

When it comes to ice and snow travel and sports, UK tourists first think of destinations in Europe or at most Canada, Nigel Hamilton, who runs a small travel agency in the UK, told Yicai, adding that only a few think of China. He believes that the most important thing for Chinese ice and snow tourism to open up the UK market is to do a good job in public communication and market education.

Visiting a country is the most powerful way to change people’s views, Haigh said. To get more people willing to travel to China, more public praise and positive experiences from those who have already visited the country are needed, he added.

Editor: Futura Costaglione
